question.text: If $\vec{u}, \vec{v}, \bar{w}$ are non-coplanar vectors and $p, q$ are real numbers, then the equality $\left[\begin{array}{llll}3 \vec{u} & p \vec{v} & p \vec{w}\end{array}\right]-\left[\begin{array}{lll}p \vec{v} & \vec{w} & q \vec{u}\end{array}\right]-\left[\begin{array}{lll}2 \vec{w} & q \vec{v} & q \vec{u}\end{array}\right]=0$ holds for

options.text: more than two but not all values of $(p, q)$
